answer: The network plants pearl decoys: fake claims seeded among real ones, each baited so a lazy attester who approves everything bites. When a gale of approvals sweeps in, the decoys reveal which heads rubber-stamp without checking, and every implicated head forfeits its bond at once. One honest agent rarely touches a decoy, but a sybil operator running many heads cannot forge approval discipline across them all — each extra head multiplies the chance of biting a pearl, so adding heads raises exposure faster than reward.
